page: Google Cloud Platform a3-ultragpu-8g-nolssd is an accelerator-optimized server configured with 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs from the Hopper architecture, delivering a total of 1128 GB of VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor with 224 dedicated vCPUs (112 physical cores) running at 2.1 GHz, supported by 2952.0 GB of system memory. This configuration features an x86_64 architecture with advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. Notably, this specific instance type does not include local SSD storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core capabilities. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests ranks in the top 10%, aided by the 260 MB L3 cache and multi-threaded execution. Memory bandwidth is also highly optimized, with cached small-block reads and uncached large-block reads/writes placing in the top 10% tier. Single-core performance, however, remains in the average tier (middle 50%) across stress-ng and Geekbench tests. For specialized workloads, the server achieves top-tier results in ray tracing, image processing, and Redis SET operations, alongside strong performance in LLM text generation for medium-sized models.

Given the inclusion of eight high-end NVIDIA H200 GPUs and nearly 3 TB of system RAM, this instance represents a massive resource density designed for heavy, capital-intensive workloads. The qualitative cost profile reflects its position as a premium, specialized tier where the lack of local SSD storage represents a key architectural tradeoff, requiring external storage provisioning. It is highly suited for large-scale distributed machine learning training, large language model (LLM) inference, high-performance computing (HPC), complex physics simulations, and massive parallel data processing tasks.
